overallNotes: Section 7.2(c) is a permission (basket) under the umbrella prohibition of Section 7.2 for incurrence of Indebtedness secured by Liens permitted by Section 7.3(g), subject to a pro forma compliance condition with the Section 7.1 financial covenants. The Section 7.1 covenants are themselves separately-owned rules (not part of the submitted operative text) and their thresholds are accordingly NOT restated in this rule to avoid double-counting; the condition is carried as a cross-rule OTHER_RULE_SATISFIED condition referencing Section 7.1 with the pro forma evaluation basis from the source's own words.

The three Section 7.1 financial ratios (Senior Secured Leverage, Total Leverage, Interest Coverage) plus the Liquidity test in Section 7.1(d) are all referenced collectively by 'the financial covenants contained in Section 7.1'. Because Section 7.1 is owned by its own candidate and its contents are not the submitted source text, the condition references Section 7.1 as a whole (ALL_SATISFIED across the referenced family) without restating its thresholds.

The Parent Borrower and its Subsidiaries is the measurement group named for the financial-covenant recomputation date; it does not widen entityScope, which identifies the obligor/actor (the Parent Borrower) that must be in compliance.

findings.verifierReasoning: The source authorizes only Indebtedness that is secured by Liens permitted by Section 7.3(g), subject to the Section 7.1 pro forma compliance proviso. The proposed IR drops the Section 7.3(g) limitation entirely, so it would treat any incurrence of debt as permitted under Section 7.2(c) so long as the Parent Borrower is in pro forma compliance with Section 7.1. A concrete divergence: unsecured debt, or debt secured by a Lien not permitted by Section 7.3(g), would be disallowed by the source but would satisfy the proposed IR's unlimited capacity and single Section 7.1 condition. This materially expands the scope and capacity of the carve-out and would change a covenant reviewer's compliance conclusion. The IR's COMPLETE sufficiency claim is therefore not supported.
